data.install_app: Install the HA TV PiP Plus app on this TV first (needs USB debugging or Wireless debugging on)

user.description:
Add a TV by its IP address.

**Find the TV's IP address:** on the TV, open Settings > Network & Internet, select the Wi-Fi network (or Ethernet) you're connected to, and look for IP address (it looks like 192.168.1.50). On some TVs it's under Settings > System > About > Status. If you can, reserve that address for the TV in your router so it doesn't change.

**Turn on developer options (needed to install the app from here):**
1. On the TV, open Settings > System > About (on some TVs: Settings > Device Preferences > About).
2. Select Android TV OS build (or Build) 7 times, until it says you're a developer.
3. Go back to Settings > System > Developer options and turn on USB debugging (on some TVs it's called Network debugging or ADB debugging). Newer Google TVs may only offer Wireless debugging; that works too, and Home Assistant walks you through it.

Then tick "Install the HA TV PiP Plus app on this TV first" and Home Assistant installs, sets up and pairs the app for you. If the app is already on the TV, leave it unticked and type the code the TV shows.
user.title: Add HA TV PiP Plus receiver

install_app.title: Install the app on the TV
install_app.description:
Home Assistant will install the latest HA TV PiP Plus app on {host}, allow it to show popups over other apps, open it, and pair with it automatically. No pairing code needed.

Before you continue, on the TV:
1. Open Settings > System > About and click the build number 7 times to turn on developer options.
2. Open Settings > System > Developer options and turn on USB debugging.

After you click Submit, watch the TV: accept the 'Allow debugging?' prompt and tick 'Always allow'. Installing takes up to a minute. You can turn USB debugging off again afterwards.

turn_tv_on.title: Turn this TV on for popups?
turn_tv_on.description:
Home Assistant can turn {name} on when a popup comes in and back off afterwards. To do that it needs the TV's Android TV Remote in Home Assistant.

{found}

**To pair the Android TV Remote** (one time, about a minute):
1. Open [Add Android TV Remote]({pair_remote_url}) in a new tab (or Settings > Devices & services > Add integration > Android TV Remote).
2. Enter this TV's IP address: {host}.
3. Type the code that appears on the TV.
4. Come back here and pick the new remote entity below.

On the TV, also turn on any quick start, network standby or wake on network setting so it can be woken over the network. You can change all of this later on the TV's Configure page, including turning it on only during set hours.

adb_server.title: This TV needs Wireless debugging
adb_server.description:
Home Assistant couldn't reach {host} with USB debugging. Newer Google TVs only allow **Wireless debugging**, which needs a pairing code.

To use it, Home Assistant installs a small helper app, **HA TV PiP Plus ADB server**, and adds this project's app repository to your app store. It runs only inside Home Assistant and publishes no ports on your network.

Click Submit to install it. This takes a minute or two.

wireless_pair.title: Pair with Wireless debugging
wireless_pair.description:
On {host}:
1. Open Settings > System > Developer options and turn on **Wireless debugging**.
2. Select **Wireless debugging**, then **Pair device with pairing code**.
3. Type the six-digit code below while it's still on the TV's screen.

Home Assistant finds the ports on its own. If it can't, fill them in from the TV: the pairing port is next to the IP address under the code, and the connection port is next to the IP address on the Wireless debugging screen.

After pairing, Home Assistant installs the app and sets it up. That takes up to a minute.

data_description.send_test_popup: Right after you save, your doorbell camera pops up with its door button, just like a real ring (the TV is turned on if your turn-on setting allows it). The button is only a test: pressing it shows a notification in Home Assistant and never unlocks or opens anything. Do not disturb is ignored for the test. Without a door-button camera, a short test video is shown.

Pausing works with most streaming apps (they pause and resume); some live-TV apps may ignore it. Mute silences the TV while the popup is up and unmutes it afterwards (needs TV app 1.37.3 or newer).

This needs the TV's Android TV Remote: if it isn't paired yet, open [Add Android TV Remote](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/config_flow_start/?domain=androidtv_remote), enter the TV's IP address and type the code the TV shows, then pick it as the TV power entity below.

data_description.power_entity: A media player or remote that switches this TV on and off. Leave empty to never turn the TV on.
data_description.wake_tv: Never: popups only show if the TV is already on. Always: turn it on any time. On a schedule: only between the two times below.
data_description.wake_tv_start: Used when "On a schedule" is chosen. If the end is earlier than the start, the window runs past midnight.
data_description.wake_tv_end: Used when "On a schedule" is chosen.
data_description.woken_tv_view: Some TVs take a while after turning on before live video shows. A still grabbed right away shows who was at the door the moment the popup was triggered. Only used when this TV was off and Home Assistant turned it on.
data_description.still_zoom: 1× shows the whole picture. Zoom in to make a face easier to see; the live video is never zoomed.
data_description.still_focus: The part of the picture to zoom into. On most doorbells, faces are in the top middle.
data_description.still_fisheye_cameras: Cameras with a round, fisheye picture (common on doorbells). Their still is flattened into a normal picture; zoom and aim then choose which part of the scene to show. Tick "Send a test popup" to see the result on this TV.
data_description.still_use_event_image: Some cameras (Eufy, for example) save their own picture of each event, often centred on the person. When it was updated around the time of the popup, it's shown as-is instead of the still below, without zoom or flattening. Otherwise the normal still is used.

camera_buttons.name: Door buttons (all TVs)
camera_buttons.description: Pair a camera with the lock, garage door, script, or button it should control. Whenever that camera pops up on a TV, the popup gets one button for it: locks unlock, covers open, and scripts or buttons run. The popup takes remote focus, and the button needs two presses. These pairings are shared by all your TVs. Leave a row empty to remove it. Tip: point the button at a script if you want extra safety checks before it runs.

appearance.name: Popups, buttons and updates (all TVs)
appearance.description:
Settings shared by every TV. Changes apply to the next popup; no app update needed. Automations can still set popup text or duration per popup.

Popup duration applies unless an automation or the TV's own default duration sets one. Width and height of 0 use the built-in size (640 × 360). Button defaults match Home Assistant's dashboard tiles. Pausing works with most streaming apps (they pause and resume); some live-TV apps may ignore it.

Install the Android APK and Home Assistant integration from the same GitHub Release before troubleshooting playback, pairing, or remote receiver issues.

receiver_overlay_permission.title: {receiver} can't show door buttons
receiver_overlay_permission.description:
The HA TV PiP Plus app on {receiver} isn't allowed to display over other apps, so popups open full screen without buttons.

To fix it, open the TV's device page in Home Assistant and press **Grant Overlay Permission** (USB debugging must be on in the TV's developer options; accept the 'Allow debugging?' prompt on the TV the first time). Or, on the TV, open HA TV PiP Plus and select **Overlay Settings**.
